intervals.label: operation (superconducting synchrotron)
intervals.note: Month precision: 51 runs were performed since March 1993; it serves as the main accelerator of the NICA complex (Nuclotron-M modernisation continues; June 2026: modernisation of the Booster, Nuclotron, collider and beam transport channel).
intervals.quote: 51 runs of the Nuclotron operation were performed since March 1993

name: Nuclotron
notes: The commissioning year (March 1993) is from the 2015 HIAT paper; the modernisation known as Nuclotron-M is part of the NICA project and is not recorded as a separate interval.

beam_energy.display: up to 6 AGeV for light ions (Z/A ~ 0.5)
beam_energy.note: Kinetic energy per nucleon for light ions; heavy ions with Z/A ~ 0.4 reach 4.5 AGeV.
beam_energy.quote: The Nuclotron will provide the experiment with beams of a variety of particles, from protons to gold ions, with kinetic energy in the range from 1 to 6 AGeV for light ions with a Z/A ratio of ∼ 0.5 and up to 4.5 AGeV for heavy ions with a Z/A ratio of ∼ 0.4.

summary.plain: The Nuclotron is JINR's superconducting ring accelerator in Dubna, in operation since 1993. It supplies protons and ions up to gold at several GeV per nucleon to fixed-target experiments such as BM@N and injects the NICA collider.
summary.technical: Nuclotron: superconducting synchrotron (cold-iron fast-cycling magnets) in operation since March 1993, delivering beams from protons to gold ions at 1-6 AGeV (light ions) and up to 4.5 AGeV (heavy ions) to BM@N and, via the Booster chain, to the NICA collider.
